scope: Thermodynamics/transonic/startline phase audit after nine-PDF ingestion gate

findings.title: T1 needs a separate error gate for approximate transonic starting data
findings.claim: A frozen variable-cp characteristic march can be admitted after KL at gamma* and comparison with zoned Sauer, source-flow order, and downstream mass conservation.

evidence.title: Engineering and Programming Manual: Two-Dimensional Kinetic Reference Computer Program (TDK)
evidence.authors: G. R. Nickerson, L. D. Dang, D. E. Coats
evidence.quote: With the above assumptions equations 2.3-1 through 2.3-11 reduce to the equations governing the irrotational flow of a perfect gas.

evidence.title: Transonic Flow in Small Throat Radius of Curvature Nozzles
evidence.quote: small perturbation transonic solution for irrotational, perfect gas flow

findings.rationale: KL(gamma*) and zoned Sauer are approximate perfect-gas-based initializations. Their mutual agreement, a downstream exact-oracle convergence rate, or conservation of their input mass flux does not bound variable-cp transonic initialization bias. The extension plan itself says the Levine-Coats small-change estimate excludes cp(T); T1 acceptance does not close this acknowledged dependency. This is an admission-evidence gap, not proof that gamma* initialization is inaccurate for every case.
findings.correction: Split T1 into consistent smooth-core verification and start-data admission. Require matched variable-cp transonic Euler/reference comparisons of sonic surface, initial p,T,V, mass flux and downstream functionals, with independent start-location/series/property-grid refinement and a declared initialization-error budget. Until then mark KL(gamma*) provisional and restrict its calibrated domain.

findings.title: Restore TDK nondimensional coordinates before using its chemistry source
findings.claim: The printed TDK source A and species equations use x in the same notation as the dimensional flow geometry.

evidence.title: TDK Engineering and Programming Manual
evidence.quote: where the coordinates (r,x) have been normalized with the throat radius.

findings.rationale: TDK keeps dimensional production rates and inserts r* because xhat=x/r*. The plan retains r* in A and dci but omits the coordinate normalization. A is dimensionless; multiplying it by dimensional dx would be inconsistent. The neighboring smooth characteristic source has units 1/length. No finite-rate production implementation was identified, so this is a specification ambiguity with a concrete scale-factor failure mode.
findings.correction: Write xhat=x/r*, rhat=r/r* explicitly and keep the TDK normalized set throughout; or use dimensional x and remove r* from A and the species transport coefficient. Add a scale-invariance/dimensional-units check to T3.

findings.title: Distinguish thermodynamic smoothing from legacy parity
findings.claim: T0 needs a shape-preserving C1 cp table while frozen Q1D stations agree to 1e-9; T1 also reduces bitwise to constant gamma.

evidence.title: Current implementation
evidence.quote: Return h(to)-h(from) = integral(cp dT) exactly per segment.

evidence.title: Implementation counterexample (project calculation, not literature data)

findings.rationale: The existing piecewise-linear cp is a thermodynamically consistent representation; h and s are already C1 when cp is continuous. Smoothing cp across its knots can be useful for higher derivatives but changes the constitutive approximation. PCHIP through cp=[1000,1200,1300] at T=[300,500,700] changes integral h from470000 to473333.333 J/kg. Thus tight legacy parity is not guaranteed merely by keeping the nodes. Bitwise parity of an interpolated/integrated branch with an analytic closed form likewise needs explicit dispatch; physics only requires a controlled limiting agreement.
findings.correction: Specify which quantities need which derivative orders. Preserve the legacy piecewise-linear adapter for exact parity; identify a smoother backend as a separate property representation, derive h,s from it, and assess its error against the same EOS or a refined property reference. Require bitwise parity only for an explicit analytic constant-cp dispatch; otherwise declare numerical tolerance and property-grid/quadrature convergence.

findings.title: Define the finite-rate equilibrium-limit test as a singular relaxation limit
findings.claim: T3 acceptance includes an unspecified equilibrium trend.

evidence.title: Characteristics of the equations of motion of a reacting gas
evidence.quote: One could conjecture that the characteristic speeds would in some way change continuously ... but this appears not to be true.

findings.rationale: Broer distinguishes convergence of resolved flow toward equilibrium from the characteristic speeds of the unreduced finite-rate PDE. For every finite rate the characteristics remain frozen; the exact-equilibrium reduced equations have equilibrium speeds. The plan states the frozen result correctly, but leaves its equilibrium acceptance and refinement order undefined. Requiring frozen characteristic angles to converge to equilibrium angles would be wrong. No existing implementation defect is asserted.
findings.correction: Define separate tests for finite-rate frozen eigenvalues, relaxation conservation and resolved/macroscopic equilibrium convergence as rate and spatial/source-step resolution change. State the limiting variables, boundary data, order of limits and supported acoustic modes. Retain chemistry stiffness/error diagnostics.

findings.title: Apply CD<=1 at the geometric throat and bind curved-start flux to it
findings.claim: The pointwise area-Mach relation directly proves that any start-line coefficient above one indicates a defect.

evidence.title: Transonic Flow in Small Throat Radius of Curvature Nozzles
evidence.quote: The ratio of the mass flow through the nozzle to the one-dimensional mass flow (discharge coefficient)

findings.rationale: The physical upper bound holds for matched uniform stagnation conditions and the same minimum throat area: at the throat rho*u_n<=rho*|V|<=rho_star*a_star, then integrate over At. A curved C-minus surface has a different area, so its equality to throat mass flux additionally requires a closed steady mass balance, oriented flux, correct normalization and controlled quadrature/series error. calc_massflow_along_rrc sums absolute segment contributions. Its scalar value alone does not establish that control-volume equivalence. Independent source sign and normalization evidence still establishes the production defects; this caveat does not rescue them. Eq14 at gamma1.23,R1.5 gives CD=0.99442694, consistent with V3 about0.9944.
findings.correction: Use the throat-normal flux proof and list assumptions. Compare source Eq14, a throat-plane integral and signed curved-start flux under refinement, with a numerical allowance. Describe CD>1 as a mass-flux consistency failure pending attribution rather than a proof identifying an individual series coefficient.
